heard: Billions of starless rogue planets drift through total darkness. These strange worlds roam across the vast expanse of the Milky Way galaxy entirely alone. Free-floating planetary masses are not bound to any star or brown dwarf. Some form on their own within stellar nurseries, while others are violently ejected from natal systems. In December 2021, astronomers found a group of up to 170 rogue planets. In September 2020, astronomers reported the detection of an Earth-mass rogue planet named Ogle 2016 BLG 1928. NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will use microlensing to reveal hundreds more. Billions of starless rogue planets drift through total darkness.
